title: Shallow Passive Decorators
pattern: A decorator/wrapper struct that implements a trait by forwarding every single method call to the wrapped type with zero modifications.
why_bad: It adds cognitive weight, nesting complexity, and instantiation boilerplate without adding any behavior, logging, safety, or transformation.
detection: Struct implementing a trait by forwarding all calls directly to an inner type implementing the same trait.
counterexample: Decorators that add dynamic behavior, like logging, buffering, or encryption, in at least one of the trait methods.
fix: Remove the decorator layer and use the wrapped type directly.
source: Michael C. Feathers, *Working Effectively with Legacy Code* (2013), Chapter 7 ("Wrap Class"), p. 225.
